keyVerseText: Go and say unto David, Thus saith the LORD, I offer thee three things; choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew root נָטַל (nâṭal) is a primitive root verb primarily conveying the action of lifting or bearing. Its core sense involves physically lifting up or carrying a weight, which metaphorically extends to bearing burdens or offering something. This literal sense of raising or taking up enriches the common English glosses like 'offer' or 'bear' by emphasizing an active, deliberate action of support or presentation rather than a passive state.
usageInScripture: The word נָטַל appears four times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently involving the notions of lifting, offering, or bearing. Its translations range from 'I offer' to 'he bare' and 'behold he taketh up,' illustrating a semantic field that includes both physical and figurative lifting or carrying. This consistency reveals the word’s flexibility in describing God’s action in bearing His people or offering choices, as well as human acts of lifting or presenting.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding נָטַל as an active lifting or bearing enriches our grasp of God's relationship to His people, portraying Him not as distant but as one who carries and sustains. The word’s emphasis on bearing burdens aligns with biblical themes of divine provision and care, foreshadowing the New Testament revelation of Christ bearing our sins. It also highlights the believer’s call to offer themselves and their lives in service, reflecting the dynamic interaction between God’s sustaining power and human response in faith.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 24:12, the LORD says to David, 'I offer thee three things; choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.' Here, נָטַל conveys the idea of God lifting or presenting options to David, emphasizing God's sovereign initiative in offering blessings or judgments. This use underscores the gracious and purposeful nature of God's actions, inviting human response to His lifted offer.
